title: Always open Twitch in theatre mode
question: How do I make Twitch always open in theater mode?
answer: Twitch has a theatre mode button and an Alt+T shortcut, but it opens each channel in the normal layout. The usermods script on this page presses the player's Theatre Mode button for you whenever you open a channel, so the video fills the window with chat beside it. Install it with usermods or any userscript manager. Without an extension, press Alt+T or click the theatre button at the bottom right of the player.
prompt: Make Twitch switch to theatre mode automatically whenever I open a stream.
details:
The script waits for the main player to appear and clicks its own **Theatre Mode** button once per page. It finds the button by the `alt+t` shortcut in its label, which Twitch uses in every language.

If you leave theatre mode, the script leaves it off until you open another page. The check loads a 24-hour channel logged out; VOD pages use the same player, but the check doesn't load one.

alternatives.title: Keyboard shortcut
alternatives.body: Press **Alt+T** (Option+T on a Mac) on a channel page, or click the theatre button at the bottom right of the player.

check.expect: (() => { const p = document.querySelector('.persistent-player'); const r = document.querySelector('[data-a-target="video-player"]').getBoundingClientRect(); return !!p && p.classList.contains('persistent-player--theatre') && r.left < 5 && r.top < 5 && r.width > 900; })()
check.intact: new Promise((done) => { const v = document.querySelector('[data-a-target="video-player"] video'); if (!v || !v.checkVisibility()) return done(false); const t0 = v.currentTime; const end = Date.now() + 10000; const tick = () => { if (!v.paused && v.currentTime > t0 + 0.5) return done(true); if (Date.now() > end) return done(false); setTimeout(tick, 250); }; tick(); })
